unverifiable_exemptions: Owner occupying the home and renting to one additional person (general FEHA exemption allowing such owners to exclude applicants based on protected characteristics)
coverage.summary: Applies statewide under FEHA to most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums and apartments. Housing providers must comply, including landlords, apartment managers and tenant screening companies. An owner occupying a home who rents to one additional person is generally exempt from FEHA, and an address lookup cannot verify this.

evidence.quoted_span: The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments
When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.

This includes landlords, homeowners, apartment managers, real estate brokers, state or local governments, owners of short-term rentals, appraisers, tenant screening companies, homeowners associations, mortgage lending companies, and public housing authorities.
Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

result.notes: I removed the summary's reference to Berkeley BMC ch. 13.106 and the claim that stricter local fair-chance ordinances operate alongside the state rule, because no document supports either; yields_to_local_rule and may_preempt_local_rules stay null. I set requires_unknown_facts to false because FEHA covers ordinary rental housing. The owner-occupied 'one additional person' exemption is a general FEHA exemption stated in the CRD FAQ; whether it reaches the criminal-history regulations specifically should be confirmed against the regulation text, which was not captured. I did not set owner_occupied_exemption_max_units because the exemption is framed as renting to one person, not as a unit count.
